note: Description taken from Sands' 1965 revision (in English), based on the soldier only; the alate is still unknown (Sands discusses possible correspondences with N. camerunensis and N. chrysopleura but could not decide). The original description is Wasmann 1911 (Kasai, Sankuru, Congo). The OCR misread decimal points as hyphens or colons (e.g. I-39 for 1.39, 0:79 for 0.79), restored here by magnitude; illegible means are not cited.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Unique among the African species: nasus short and thick (nasus cone angle 18—30 degrees), only 4 bristles at the tip of the nasus and 2 or 4 bristles in a transverse row at the base of the nasus; bristles of the postmental plate confined to the anterior margin. It went unrecognized for a long time after its 1911 description, until Sands found new material.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule ferruginous orange to chestnut-brown, nasus deep chestnut-brown to brownish black with a red tip; pronotum, antennae and abdominal tergites yellowish brown; legs yellow, sternites pale yellow. Head capsule almost circular in frontal view, nasus broadly conical; in lateral view nearly straight or slightly wavy from well behind the base of the nasus, then rising and passing smoothly into the back of the head, often with a small elevation at the base of the nasus; nasus distinctly shorter than the rest of the head capsule measured from the posterior margin of the antennal bases, nasus cone angle 18—30 degrees; postmental plate weakly convex; antennae 13-segmented, II and V about equal and longer than IV but shorter than III. Cephalic bristles: 1 pair on the vertex, 2 or 4 in a transverse row at the base of the nasus, 4 at the tip of the nasus, and several on the anterior margin of the postmental plate, plus minute bristles on the vertex visible only at a particular angle of illumination. Abdominal tergites with very sparse minute bristles, longer at the posterior margins, 4 per segment in longitudinal rows; sternites sparsely and shortly bristled, the posterior marginal bristles longer and less regularly arranged than on the tergites. Measurements (17 heads, 4 localities, mm): head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.39—1.58 (mean 1.49); head width 0.79—1.00 (mean 0.92); head capsule depth 0.54—0.65 (mean 0.61); pronotum width 0.41—0.50 (mean 0.44); pronotum length 0.15—0.20; hind tibia length 0.95—1.08 (mean 1.02).
